items.statement: A self-adjoint real matrix bounded above by the identity satisfies the exponential quadratic bound for every positive parameter.

formulae.label: One-sided real matrix exponential quadratic bound
formulae.tex: A=A^\top,\quad A\preceq I,\quad s>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad e^{sA}\preceq I+sA+(e^s-s-1)A^2.

assumptions: The public result concerns a real square matrix on any finite nonempty index set. The order \(U\preceq V\) means that \(V-U\) is positive semidefinite as a full quadratic form. The matrix exponential is the matrix-algebra power series.

The public mathematical hypotheses are precisely \(A=A^\top\), \(I-A\succeq0\), and \(s>0\). The cap is one-sided; negative eigenvalues are unrestricted. Finite enumeration and decidable equality supply the Lean matrix index structure.

Private actual-use scope: take \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), \(r=q+1\), \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), and the original unconditional measure \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\), where \(\gamma_j=N(0,I_j)\). The case \(q=0\) is included.

For source indices \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\Phi_i=(\omega_b(i))_{b=0}^q\), \(\theta_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i=(1,\sqrt2\cos\theta_i,\ldots,\sqrt2\cos(q\theta_i))\), and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). Lean uses source index \(i.val+1\).

Set \(Y_i=d^{-1}(\Phi_i\Phi_i^\top\otimes t_it_i^\top)\mathbf1_{\{\|\Phi_i\|^2\le L\}}\), \(M_i=\int Y_i\,d\mu\), \(Z_i=Y_i-M_i\), \(\rho=2r(L+1)/d\), and \(X_i=\rho^{-1}Z_i\). The paired matrix index lists the Gaussian coordinate first and the feature coordinate second. Norms use the real Euclidean operator norm with its standard Borel structure.

For this private consumer, the sole dimension hypothesis and these literal definitions determine every object. Positivity of \(\rho\), centering, Hermitian structure, measurability, integrability and the spectral cap are proved internally. All expectations use the same original \(\mu\); no all-row good event or conditional law is introduced.

assumption_deltas.source: The proof of Lemma6.7 uses the deterministic cap X≼I for self-adjoint matrices in a complex finite-dimensional setting.
assumption_deltas.lean: A is real Hermitian on any finite nonempty index set, with full PSD(I-A) and s>0.
assumption_deltas.reason: The explicit real restriction is sufficient for the actual Gaussian matrices. This binding covers the deterministic component, not the full complex random theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The scalar remainder has value s²/2 at zero and is increasing on the real line.
assumption_deltas.lean: The integral representation proves this across all real arguments, including negative eigenvalues and zero.
assumption_deltas.reason: No two-sided norm cap or PSD(A) assumption replaces the one-sided source cap.

assumption_deltas.source: Gaussian source summands are actually centered, bounded by R_*, and live under their original law.
